parts.visual:
Startup A builds a $10/month app. They spend $15 on marketing to acquire a user. They go bankrupt in 3 months. 
Startup B builds a $100,000/year Enterprise software. They take 9 months to close a single deal. They run out of cash and go bankrupt.

The Pricing Model:
1. The Math of Survival: Pricing is not just a number on a website; it dictates your entire product architecture, your marketing strategy, and the type of salespeople you must hire.
2. B2C vs B2B: Business-to-Consumer (B2C) relies on millions of users paying tiny amounts (Spotify). Business-to-Business (B2B) relies on a few massive companies paying huge amounts (Salesforce). The product management required for each is completely different.
parts.audio: Pricing is a product feature. If you design a brilliant enterprise tool but try to sell it for $5 a month with a self-serve checkout, large corporations will actually refuse to buy it because it looks 'too cheap to be secure.'

questions.question: What is the psychological trap of the 'Freemium' model?
options: The Free-Rider Problem. You offer a great free version hoping users will upgrade to Pro. But if the free version is TOO good, 99% of users will never pay you a dime, and your server costs will bankrupt the company.
questions.correct_answer: The Free-Rider Problem. You offer a great free version hoping users will upgrade to Pro. But if the free version is TOO good, 99% of users will never pay you a dime, and your server costs will bankrupt the company.
questions.explanation: You must find the exact point of pain that forces them to pay.

questions.question: Listen to the Enterprise PM. Why does an Enterprise product look so 'boring' compared to a consumer app?
questions.tts_text: My enterprise buyers don't care about cute animations. They care about single sign-on security, compliance with European data laws, and admin permission roles. They are paying me $50,000 to keep them out of jail, not to entertain them.
options: Compliance over Delight. In B2B Enterprise, the person using the software is rarely the person paying for it. The buyer is a CTO who requires strict security features (SSO, Audit Logs). If you don't have those, the deal is dead instantly.
questions.correct_answer: Compliance over Delight. In B2B Enterprise, the person using the software is rarely the person paying for it. The buyer is a CTO who requires strict security features (SSO, Audit Logs). If you don't have those, the deal is dead instantly.
questions.explanation: Sell to the buyer, build for the user.

questions.question: What is a 'Paywall'?
options: A digital barrier in the product flow. For example, a news website lets you read 3 articles for free. When you click the 4th, a screen pops up demanding a credit card. It is the literal boundary between free value and revenue.
questions.correct_answer: A digital barrier in the product flow. For example, a news website lets you read 3 articles for free. When you click the 4th, a screen pops up demanding a credit card. It is the literal boundary between free value and revenue.

questions.question: What does 'Product-Led Growth' (PLG) mean?
options: The product sells itself. Instead of hiring salespeople to call clients, you build a product so incredibly intuitive and valuable that users invite their own coworkers to use it (like Slack or Notion). The product acts as the sales engine.
questions.correct_answer: The product sells itself. Instead of hiring salespeople to call clients, you build a product so incredibly intuitive and valuable that users invite their own coworkers to use it (like Slack or Notion). The product acts as the sales engine.

pairs.match: Giving 90% of the value for free, charging for the final 10%
Selling massive $100k contracts requiring high security and compliance
Designing the software to automatically sell itself and spread via users
